title: From Agent Traces to Agent Simulations — Rustem Feyzkhanov, Snorkel AI
talk_summary: Snorkel's AI platform lead argues that production traces alone can't support repeatable agent comparison, so you should convert traces into simulation benchmark tasks (instruction.md + Docker environment + hidden Oracle solution + verifiers) and run them offline as a release gate. The benchmark is treated as software with its own CI, populated continuously from production failures, and used to test the full agent stack (model, prompt, harness, tools) rather than just the model.

takeaways.what_they_do: Convert production traces into repeatable offline tasks with a fixed environment, an Oracle solution proving solvability, and verifiers, so different agent configs can be compared apples-to-apples.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Offline simulation turns traces into repeatable experiments. Now you take production traces, you construct tasks
takeaways.numbers: millions of agent simulations per month

takeaways.technique: Full-stack config comparison on fixed environment
takeaways.what_they_do: Hold environment and evaluators constant while varying model, thinking level, prompt, harness, and tools, then compare on cost, latency, and retries, not just pass rate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can change the prompt. You can tune the full hardness and skills tools available to agent

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat benchmark tasks as code with a separate CI pipeline: pin dependencies, check base images and fixtures, run Oracle to confirm it passes, run agents to confirm solvable-but-hard, tag difficulty, then approve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: benchmark is software. It's code. It's files. You need to treat it as such. You need to have a separate CI pipeline

takeaways.what_they_do: Don't have experts review everything; route only cases where agent and verifiers disagree (task thought solved but marked failed, or trace judged suboptimal) to subject-matter experts to tune the judge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you specifically want to find cases where there's disagreement between agent and different verifiers

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep an expansion loop (production traces/failures become new benchmark tasks) and a simulation loop (run experiments, record, gate release), explicitly connecting observability and experimentation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's important to under- to make sure that your observability piece and experimentation piece are connected

takeaways.what_they_do: Run agent in one container with sidecar containers for mocked APIs, DB snapshots, and MCP tools, plus simulated LLM users, instead of full production; multi-step prompts/verifiers allow early exit on long-horizon tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You don't run the full production database. You have a certain snapshot. You can run side containers sidecars
